# #4850: Patch: `classify --claims` sees a script change to a card's Radiant face, by playing its forced games with the card Radiant too
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

`classify --claims` confirms a script-only change by playing 40 plain games (seeds 1 to 40) with the card forced into both decks, on the branch's build and on the base's, and counting where they diverge (`crates/tools/src/classify.rs:950-975`, `forced_games_diverge`; the games come from `crates/tools/src/golden.rs:394-399`, `record_game`, which builds `CreateGameArgs { seed, decks, handicaps, ..default }` with no deck marks).

In a plain game a card is Radiant only by an in-game upgrade, so those games almost never run a card's Radiant face:

- Core #2 Speciesist (`core-002`): resolved in 36 of the 40 games, **never on its Radiant face**; a Radiant copy exists in 1 game.
- Three other cards sampled the same way: `classic-004` Radiant in 1 of 40, `stinkyscape-094` 1 of 40, `meditative-040` 3 of 40.

So a change to Speciesist's Radiant Cry (`destroy_all`, against the base face's `destroy`) cannot diverge. `checked.scripts` stays empty and the change reads as Internal. `--claims` then asks for no patch fragment, and an honest `--plays core-002` fails with "claims "core-002" plays differently, but its games against the base build play as before (R1370000)". A real card change merges with no patch entry, and the true claim is refused.

The premise is proven by the test. The consequence is by reading (`claims.rs:71-75`, `:86-98`), with high confidence; it was not run end to end against a base build.

### What should happen

- R1365000: "A card plays differently when … its script's code changes".
- R3935001 already treats this class as a defect: "`classify --claims` read the change as playing as before and a fragment could not claim it. This amends that check."
- The fuzz gate closed the same gap for itself in #4161 (`crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs:644-647`: "The plain wave's copies are Radiant only by an in-game upgrade, so this small second batch pins them Radiant").

### How to reproduce

Fails on `main` (3a83bd7): `classify_forced_games_play_the_forced_cards_radiant_face`, in [`crates/tools/tests/audit_tools.rs` at b5a9801](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/b5a9801/crates/tools/tests/audit_tools.rs) (branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`). It runs `jackioh golden record --seeds 1..40 --force core-002 --out <tmp>`, which is exactly what `record_seeds(1..=FORCED_GAMES, [id], [])` records, folds each game again with `create_game`, `begin_game` and `reduce`, and counts `GameEvent::CardResolved { def_id == "core-002", radiant: Some(true) }`.

```rust
let (games, resolved, resolved_radiant, held_radiant) = forced_games("core-002");
assert_eq!(games, 40);
assert!(resolved > 0, "the control: the forced games play the card");
assert!(resolved_radiant > 0, "none of classify's forced games resolves it Radiant …");
```

Run with `JACKIOH_AUDIT_TMP=<a scratch directory> cargo test -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/testkit --test audit_tools`.

Output today: `core-002: 40 forced games, resolved in 36, resolved Radiant in 0, a Radiant copy held in 1`.

### Where

CI, deploys or tooling: `crates/tools/src/classify.rs` (`forced_games_diverge`), `crates/tools/src/golden.rs` (`record_game`).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- When the plain forced games show no divergence, record a second batch with the forced cards pinned Radiant (deck marks carried in the recorded `args`, as `GameSetup::radiant` does for the fuzz's Radiant rotation) and count its divergences the same way. Only when the first batch is quiet, so the common case costs what it does now.
- The recorded games' format gains the marks: check `golden check` and the hotseat fixture still fold (`MatchConfig::fold_args` carries `deckMarks` for the AI's matches already, #1697).
- A ruling note amending R1370000 (as R3935001 amended it before), in this issue's block.
- A limit that R1365000 states and this issue does not change: a divergence counts only when it touches the forced card or no card, so a changed trigger that fires during another card's action is attributed to that card. `STEERED_GAMES` covers only the three Walls.
- Latent neighbours seen by reading, to check while there: stage 1 ignores code below a file's first `#[cfg(test)]` in every Rust file, not only card scripts (`catalog.rs:1752`; no engine, cards or AI source has code below one today), and `code_changed` lexes TypeScript with the Rust lexer, so a `//` inside a single-quoted or template string hides the rest of the line (no live case under `apps/web/src/cards/`).

Found by an audit of the project's own gates (`crates/tools`); the reproduction was run and the code read before filing.
